The rest of this page uses one model, CFSv2. The
[seasonal ensemble case](seasonal-mme-2023.qmd) calibrates seven models for one start
date at 0.05°. Doing that for all twelve seasons would take several hundred fits, so
this section uses a coarser measurement that already exists: the scan made to choose
that case's start date. It fitted CCA to each of the seven models for every start
month, on a 0.25° grid, with the settings of this page (3 predictor EOFs, 3
predictand EOFs, 2 CCA modes). The rows below are its forecasts started one month
before the season, the lead used throughout this page.

| Season | CFSv2 alone | Seven-model ensemble | Best single model | Ensemble's rank | CFSv2 RPSS | Ensemble RPSS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JFM | 0.14 | 0.18 | CanSIPSIC3, 0.21 | 3 of 8 | 0.09 | 0.12 |
| FMA | 0.09 | 0.12 | SPEAR, 0.18 | 4 of 8 | 0.06 | 0.08 |
| MAM | 0.10 | 0.15 | SEAS51c, 0.22 | 4 of 8 | 0.07 | 0.10 |
| AMJ | 0.06 | 0.08 | SEAS51c, 0.12 | 3 of 8 | 0.04 | 0.06 |
| MJJ | -0.03 | 0.28 | CanSIPSIC3, 0.34 | 5 of 8 | 0.00 | 0.11 |
| JJA | 0.34 | 0.42 | GEOSS2S, 0.44 | 2 of 8 | 0.11 | 0.16 |
| JAS | 0.50 | 0.55 | GEOSS2S, 0.57 | 2 of 8 | 0.21 | 0.26 |
| ASO | 0.61 | 0.63 | SEAS51c, 0.64 | 2 of 8 | 0.34 | 0.34 |
| SON | 0.60 | 0.62 | SPEAR, 0.63 | 2 of 8 | 0.30 | 0.33 |
| OND | 0.50 | 0.56 | SEAS51c, 0.57 | 3 of 8 | 0.24 | 0.29 |
| NDJ | 0.24 | 0.28 | CESM1, 0.31 | 4 of 8 | 0.11 | 0.14 |
| DJF | 0.20 | 0.23 | SEAS51c, 0.27 | 3 of 8 | 0.10 | 0.13 |

: Cross-validated Pearson correlation and RPSS of CCA-calibrated forecasts started one month before each season, area-weighted mean over Indonesia at 0.25°, training target years 1992-2020. The ensemble is the equal-weight mean of the seven calibrated forecasts; rank 1 means above every member. Source: [skill-calendar.csv](../data/seasonal-mme-2023/skill-calendar.csv), written by `research/scripts/skill_calendar_scan.py`.

1. **The ensemble is above CFSv2 alone in all twelve seasons**, by 0.01 to 0.30 in
   correlation. The gain is 0.08 or less everywhere except MJJ, where CFSv2's
   correlation is -0.03 and four other models score about 0.3. Its RPSS is at
   least as high as CFSv2's in every season too.
2. **It is never the best, and never far from it.** One model is above the ensemble
   in every season, but the ensemble is second or third of 8 in 8 of the 12 seasons
   and never lower than 5th. The best single model changes with the season
   (5 of the 7 models are best at least once), which is why picking one in advance
   is hard.
3. **Combining models does not create skill where there is none.** The ensemble
   reaches 0.4 or more only for JJA, JAS, ASO, SON and OND, the seasons where the members are
   good too. For the other seven seasons it is 0.08 to 0.28.

Read this beside the rest of the page with care. It is a different measurement:
correlation and RPSS over the training years, not the 2023 errors scored above; a
0.25° grid, not 0.05°; training target years 1992-2020, not 1991-2020; and the
CFSv2 hindcasts of PyCPT's catalog. A cross-validated correlation of 0 is also not
the no-skill level: a forecast with no model scores -0.24 to -0.51 in these seasons
(the [ensemble page](seasonal-mme-2023.qmd#why-a-correlation-near-zero-is-not-no-skill-here)
explains why), so the comparison between columns is the safer reading.
